places.name: Alten Meerhleel
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md (Alten Meerhleel: a port built to trade with outsiders; Hist: NONE)

why.founding: An outsider-facing port north-west of Lilmoth, below city scale, where an Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. With Lilmoth destroyed for a century and a half the bay's outside trade came here, and enough of it stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm ground behind it for a warehouse row. The 'alten-' in the name means outsiders.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports. The customs presence is one clerk and a tariff shed nobody staffs. That shed is what the port sells.
why.pressures: Now that Lilmoth is rebuilt the two ports are direct rivals. Meerhleel's advantage is that it asks nothing, but Corimont, the province's real free port, asks nothing more securely.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council ever dropped its tariffs, Meerhleel would lose the only reason anyone sails past a real harbour.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes

vibe.silhouette: A straight warehouse gable-line and two masts on one side of the landing, a low uneven raft-quarter with no roofline at all on the other. Nothing between them but the stage.
vibe.palette: Sun-bleached deck timber, painted price boards, brown estuary water.
vibe.materials: Two kits sharing a stage: sawn plank, ridge-tile and iron strap in the warehouse row; lashed plank platforms on piles, reed and cane in the quarter. Nothing structural crosses the stage in either direction.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two building grammars on one waterfront: a lashed Argonian plank quarter moored to its piles, and a straight-gabled outsiders' warehouse row, sharing a landing stage and no carpentry whatsoever.
vibe.condition: Prospering and patched: the warehouse row is maintained to the day, the raft-quarter is rebuilt continuously, but it looks worse for it.
vibe.approach: From the water, masts and a warehouse gable read together before any of the plank quarter does.
vibe.senses: Cargo hooks and tallying, two argument-registers in two languages, tar and bilge and unswept spice, brown estuary smell at slack water.

ID unchanged.

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: The one firm shelf at the head of the estuary, with the stilt quarters and the lighter quay stepping down off it into tidal water. Big hulls anchor out in Oliis Bay and lighter in, and the lightering is the city's living.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; nobody wants a ruler. The last party that had one killed the city.
why.pressures: Hostile to the An-Xileel successor state and indispensable to a bay that must trade somewhere. It is also built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once. The rules forbid it.

hardConstraints: on the firm shelf at the estuary head, its quays out over tidal water

preferences.neighbourRelation: bay port with a second door (a floating port) across the water

vibe.materials: Argonian throughout above the waterline: lashed stilt timber, split-cane decking, mud-and-reed infill, thatch and hide awnings, Argonian lamp-cages. The Imperial ashlar is only what the water left standing, and nothing new is built into it.
vibe.signatureFeature: Ninety per cent Argonian stilt-and-platform work climbing high over drowned Imperial villas, inside a wall that is Imperial on three sides and Argonian facing the estuary.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt, and newer everywhere than the ground it stands on. Bright deck timber over black Imperial masonry, the joins left honest.
vibe.approach: From the bay the lamp-tiers read first, stacked above the quay; from the north road you come down off the rise and the drowned quarter is under you before you notice the water.
vibe.senses: Pole-thump and hull-knock under every walkway, the tariff bell over the quay, tar and fish-oil and drying mould; at night, wet stone rising off the drowned quarter under the floor.

places.name: The Wraxu Frieze

places.name: Wraxu Stacks
